steps.body: Any tenths amount can be renamed in hundredths: each tenth is worth 10 hundredths, so multiply the count by 10.
steps.narration: Any tenths amount can be renamed in hundredths: each tenth is worth 10 hundredths, so multiply the count by 10.

widget.prompt: Shade the grid to show 0.40. Each full column is one tenth; each cell is one hundredth.

commonCounts.feedback: That shades 4 single cells — 4 hundredths. Each TENTH is a full column of 10 cells, so 0.4 needs 4 whole columns: 40 cells.

widget.successFeedback: Four full columns — the same amount as 0.4, now counted as 40 hundredths.
widget.lowFeedback: The shaded amount is still below the target. Fill whole columns for the tenths digit first, then single cells for the hundredths.
widget.highFeedback: The shaded amount has gone past the target. Each full column is one tenth — check the tenths digit before adding single cells.

predict.prompt: 0.4 shades four full columns. Counted cell by cell, how many hundredths is that?
predict.reveal: Each column holds 10 cells, so four columns hold 4 × 10 = 40 cells — 40 hundredths. Just 4 hundredths would be four single cells — a sliver of one column, not four full columns — so the same digit names ten times less.

invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for g4d tenth to hundredth must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines g4d tenth to hundredth.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

explanationVariants: Each tenth is 10 hundredths, so 0.4 is 40/100.

widget.prompt: 0.4 = ?/100. What numerator makes the fraction name the same amount?

commonErrors.feedback: That copies the tenths count without rescaling it. Each tenth is 10 hundredths, so 4 tenths covers 4 × 10 hundredths of the same whole.
That multiplies by 100 as if 0.4 were 4 whole units. It is 4 tenths, and each tenth contains 10 hundredths, so multiply the count by 10.

0.90 is 90 hundredths, so 90 cells must be shaded.

widget.prompt: A hundredths grid has 100 equal cells. How many cells must be shaded to show 0.90?

commonErrors.feedback: That shades only the tenths digit's worth of single cells. In 0.90 the 9 sits in the tenths place, so it is worth 9 full columns — 90 cells — before the hundredths digit adds any more.
That count is one full column — ten cells — past the amount. The tenths digit of 0.90 calls for exactly 9 full columns.
